about: Terms every Prism model's documentation shares, each with a definition a newcomer can read. scripts/content/enrich.mjs links the first use of each on a page to its definition; a repository adds its own in model/content.json. `match` lists the forms that count as a use; `case` keeps the match case-sensitive.

terms.plain: A description of an app, written in LexLean, that covers every facet of it and that the Lean kernel checks before the app is built.
One view of a model, such as its architecture, its security or its quality. Each facet holds records.
One entry in a facet: a component, a threat, a measure or a journey step, with the place in the source it came from.
The language Prism models are written in. It reads like LaTeX and compiles to Lean 4.
The small checker at the heart of the Lean prover. It accepts a proof only if every step follows the rules.
A statement about the model that the Lean kernel has checked, so it holds for every input, not only the ones tested.
The app Prism builds: one signed, verified file that a browser or a device runs.
Software development kit. Here, the PrismPM container image that builds, checks and verifies Prism models.
A content address: a hash of the exact bytes a record was read from, so anyone can check where it came from.
To translate a Rust function into a LexLean definition with its proofs, so the model says what the code does.
The part of a subject not lifted yet. It is listed by name and may only shrink.
An input and the output the app must give for it. The holo replays each one before it is offered.
A way of organizing documentation into four kinds: tutorials, how-to guides, reference and explanation.
A person or group with an interest in the system, as ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 defines it.
A reader drawn from one stakeholder, with a name and a goal, so a page is written for someone in particular.
Model Context Protocol: an open protocol through which AI agents call tools such as the Prism builder.
Universal Object Reference: the UOR Foundation's framework for naming any object by its content.
A signed record of where a build came from: which source, which workflow and which inputs.
A plain-text index of a site, at its root, written for language models to read.
